clips.text: So here's the question a head of marketing with forty branches will ask. How does Ask Maps decide which of my branches to mention? Google hasn't said. It names the inputs, which are places data, community reviews and the user's own searches and saved places. It doesn't say how one business gets picked over another. So the levers you've got are your listing and your reviews. Which is local SEO with a chat window on the front. Partly. The customer asks for an outcome, a four o'clock nail appointment or a day out, and gets one plan back. If your branch isn't in it, they never saw a list with you on it.

Ask Maps, the Gemini chat in Google Maps, is coming to the UK, and its trip itineraries show whether each stop is open.

In this clip Hannah and I go through two jobs to hand over.

The first is that audit. It hands back a table of every location where the listing, the site and the plan disagree, with the correct value to set.

The second is a fortnightly check. Give AI ten to twenty requests a customer would make in your category and towns, plus the answers you collect from Maps. It sorts out which of your locations appeared, which competitors did, and anything Maps got wrong about you.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/google-ask-maps-uk-local-marketing/
clips.text: Get AI on this, first job. Audit every location's hours and details before Christmas. Give it an export of your Business Profile locations and your store finder page, plus your Christmas and New Year opening plan. It hands back a table of every location where the listing, the site and the plan disagree, with the correct value to set. Second job. Find out what Ask Maps says about you once it's on UK phones. Give it ten to twenty requests a customer would make in your category and towns, and the answers you collect from Maps. It sorts them into which of your locations appeared, which competitors did, and anything Maps said about you that's wrong. Run it fortnightly. A person still types the requests on a phone.
